A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MVP-LAM and contain readable main texts and appendices A–E. Equations, tables, figures, and relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original mutual-information estimates, action-probing results, simulated manipulation evaluations, ablations, and viewpoint-perturbation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds LIBERO-Goal policy evaluation, synchronization and scaling experiments, inverse probing, and attention analyses.

M1.justification: The DINOv2-based quantized encoder–decoder, self-view and cross-view reconstruction objectives, and VLA pretraining and action-decoding procedures remain unchanged. The added model-size and viewpoint sweeps evaluate configurations of the existing method.

E1.justification: LIBERO-Goal, previously used for representation probing, is additionally used for policy finetuning and closed-loop manipulation evaluation. Synthetic synchronization offsets add a temporal-misalignment scenario. The underlying robot/human training datasets and other benchmark coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes the OXE-pretrained UniVLA comparator, which scored 92.0% on LIBERO-Long in v1. The perturbed-action MI/probing comparison also drops LAPA and Moto, retaining only MVP-LAM and UniVLA in v2 Table 16; both dropped methods remain in reconstruction comparisons.

E3.justification: Added evaluation designs include inverse probing from actions to latents, synchronization lags of 0/2/4 frames, and sweeps over 1/2/3 viewpoints, 10/50/100% data, and 100/150/300M model sizes. These substantially expand the experimental controls; retained main training and probing protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostics with synchronization robustness, three scaling analyses, inverse probing for latent minimality, attention comparisons with/without cross-view reconstruction, and attention-based failure analysis under viewpoint perturbation. Existing human-data and reconstruction-loss ablations remain; the original perturbation analysis is partly relocated and narrowed.

E5.justification: v2 Tables 3 and 16 newly specify that perturbed trajectories are resampled for each random seed. Three-seed perturbation reporting, four-seed representation evaluations, and five-seed LIBERO evaluation are retained; an increase in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds LIBERO-Goal success rates of 94.8% for MVP-LAM and 91.9% for UniVLA, plus synchronization, scaling, inverse-probing, and attention findings. MVP-LAM's SIMPLER 60.4% and LIBERO-Long 90.8% remain unchanged. Perturbation MI/NMSE changes from 1.37/1.46 to 1.38/1.44 for MVP-LAM (v1 Figure 6; v2 Table 16), and Moto reconstruction MSE changes from 0.296 to 0.295. These are revised reports, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The action-centricity definition, mutual-information bound, Appendix A assumptions and derivation, and remaining mathematical formulations are unchanged. The new minimality discussion and inverse probing add conceptual qualifications and empirical diagnostics, not new formal theory.

C1.justification: The central cross-view learning and action-centricity claims remain. v2 extends downstream claims to LIBERO-Goal and adds explicit scalability and synchronization-robustness claims, emphasizes threefold pretraining-data efficiency, and suggests progress toward universal latent actions. It also newly claims dynamic-background robustness without an identifiable corresponding test.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies the interpretation of action-centricity: high MI and good probing do not establish minimal representations or guarantee downstream policy performance. It adds explanations of synchronization tolerance, attention localization, and failures under larger viewpoint changes. Conversely, Appendix D.2 removes v1's warning that externally reported baseline scores use differing training recipes.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-site link stating code and checkpoint availability and discloses an LPIPS-below-0.5 constraint for viewpoint sampling. The PDFs do not establish whether that constraint was newly introduced or previously undocumented. The baseline-result provenance paragraph is removed; most implementation, hardware, and hyperparameter details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of TCN, MV-MWM, and ReViWo and replaces CoLA-World with AdaWorld. References add Gao, Seo, and Pang and remove the CoLA-World and Kim fine-tuning works. The central positioning around multi-view latent-action learning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and robustness discussion receive targeted rewrites. Perturbed-action evaluation moves into Appendix E.3, explanatory paragraphs are added, and impact and acknowledgement sections appear. The overall section hierarchy and much of the method and appendix prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a broader method-and-results overview, Figure 5 adds LIBERO-Goal examples, and Table 2 is rebuilt with dataset-size and benchmark columns. v1's composite perturbation figure is redistributed into tables and an expanded image gallery. New scaling plots, attention figures, and diagnostic tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses gaps in v1 by testing synchronization sensitivity and qualifying what representation diagnostics establish, supported by inverse probing and viewpoint-failure examples. LIBERO-Goal and scaling results add useful evidence. These gains are limited by sparse scaling-protocol details, removed baseline comparisons and comparability caveats, and an unsupported dynamic-background robustness claim. Overall, the evidence and interpretation improve modestly around an unchanged method and retained headline results.
